gen-comfortaa-gf-varela-round: Varela Round has rounded, wide-mouthed lowercase and strokes of uniform width, easy company for the heading. And Comfortaa's neon-tube lines stay the showpiece, so the body can sit at a modest size.
gen-comfortaa-gf-vazirmatn: Comfortaa draws its letters like fine rope, every stroke the same and its c a wide ring, while Vazirmatn stays low-key beneath. Friendly geometry up top, a sans-serif that never tightens below.
gen-comfortaa-gf-ysabeau: Ysabeau sweeps its curves wide and never lets them close up, a plain sans with a human hand. Comfortaa's pen-plotter smoothness is the showpiece of the pair, geometric and smiling above it.
gen-comfortaa-gf-ysabeau-office: Smooth, round and drafted. Comfortaa holds the line of a technical pen, and Ysabeau Office follows with open-ended curves that keep a sans text moving through a long page without crowding.
gen-comfortaa-gf-zalando-sans-expanded: Comfortaa draws every stroke at a constant width, round and friendly. Zalando Sans Expanded spaces its sans-serif letters out with wide gaps, so a long stretch of text reads slowly and openly.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-alegreya: Aaargh is blunt and untapered, every bowl and stem cut at the same weight. Alegreya, a serif with lightly flexed contrast, is the one for sustained text, while the heading belongs big and brief.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-aref-ruqaa-ink: Aaargh keeps every stem and curve at the same width, stout and sure. Aref Ruqaa Ink is the soft counterpart, a serif whose shoulders thicken gently and whose apertures stay open.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-average: Blunt, heavy and unshaded. Aaargh has no stroke contrast at all, and Average, a text serif with a mild reed-pen swell and gaping e, lets a longer passage go down smoothly.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-besley: Aaargh draws every stroke at a single width. Besley offers what that lacks: a serif with gentle weight shifts in its bowls and thinner crossbars, made for steady reading while the heading just shouts.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-bona-nova: Bona Nova is a serif with a restrained swell and curves that hold their mouths open. Aaargh is best at blunt, uniform strokes that hit hard, while Bona Nova is best at the quiet detail of heavier stems against lighter crossbars.
